SOURCE LIMITS. The 10-K Business and MD&A sections were not available: "10-K.txt: Item 1 section was not found." and "10-K.txt: Item 7 section was not found." Only the earnings release (earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt) can be cited. Business-model detail, stated competitive advantages, revenue concentration and management's growth plans from Item 1 and Item 7 are therefore "not stated in the files." Management's growth is treated as a claim to test, and the release is the only evidence.

OVERVIEW
Costco reported fiscal 2026 results for the period ended August 30, 2026: "Costco Wholesale Corporation (“Costco” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: COST) today announced its operating results for the 16-week fourth quarter and the 52-week fiscal year ended August 30, 2026." [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L9]
The release states: "Net sales for the fiscal year increased 10.1 percent, to $297.2 billion, from $269.9 billion last year." [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L10]
Membership fees are a second revenue stream. The label reads "Membership fees" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L78], with fiscal-year values of "5,907" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L81] against "5,323" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L82], in $ millions.
Operating income for the 52 weeks was "11,685" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L102] versus "10,383" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L103]. Net income was "9,226" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L131] versus "8,099" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L133].
The fourth-quarter result carries a one-time item: "This year's fourth quarter was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values." [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L44]
Revenue concentration by customer, category or member type is "not stated in the files."
Insight: Fiscal 2026 results combine a recurring fee stream (membership fees of $5,907 million versus $5,323 million the prior year) with a one-time fourth-quarter tariff-refund benefit, so the fee line is the recurring element and the refund is not. [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L81] "5,907" and [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L44] "This year's fourth quarter was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values."

MARKET POSITIONING AND GROWTH OUTLOOK
Criterion 1, Demand durability: SUPPORTED, with gaps.
- Sales: the fourth-quarter figure is "Net sales for the quarter increased 11.2 percent, to $93.9 billion, from $84.4 billion last year." [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L10]
- Comparable sales: total company 52-week comparable sales are "8.4%" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L36]. The adjusted figure, which excludes gasoline price and foreign exchange effects, is "6.6%" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L37]. The footnote reads "*Excluding the impacts from changes in gasoline prices and foreign exchange." [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L43] Reading the table as 16-week, 16-week adjusted, 52-week, 52-week adjusted, the fourth-quarter adjusted total company comp was "6.7%" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L35].
- Membership fees: fourth-quarter fees were "1,850" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L79] versus "1,724" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L80]. Deferred membership fees on the balance sheet were "3,006" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L224] versus "2,854" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L225].
- Gaps: member count, renewal rate and traffic or ticket data are "not stated in the files." Recurring demand rests on sales, comps and fee revenue alone.

Criterion 2, Competitive position: MIXED.
- Adjusted fiscal-year comps are positive in every region: U.S. "6.6%" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L22], Canada "6.7%" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L27], Other International "6.5%" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L32]. The label for the first is "U.S." [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L18].
- Digitally-enabled comps are strong: the 52-week adjusted figure is "20.7%" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L42] under the label "Digitally-Enabled" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L38].
- Cost lines rose with sales. Merchandise costs were "264,279" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L92] versus "239,886" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L93]. SG&A was "27,190" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L97] versus "24,966" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L98].
- Management reinvested some benefit in pricing: "less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L44].
- Why mixed: competitor comparisons, market share, segment operating income and stated advantages are "not stated in the files." The regional comps show broad demand but do not isolate an advantage over competitors.

Criterion 3, Growth execution: MIXED.
- Footprint: "Costco currently operates 939 warehouses, including 647 in the United States and Puerto Rico, 115 in Canada, 43 in Mexico, 37 in Japan, 29 in the United Kingdom, 20 in Korea, 15 in Australia, 14 in Taiwan, seven in China, five in Spain, three in France, two in Sweden, and one each in Iceland, and New Zealand." [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L45] The release also says "Costco also operates e-commerce sites in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Mexico, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Australia, and China." [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L45]
- Investment: additions to property and equipment were "(6,435)" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L310] versus "(5,498)" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L311]. Net property and equipment was "35,633" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L197] versus "31,909" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L198].
- Funding: operating cash flow was "15,825" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L306] versus "13,335" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L307]. Cash and cash equivalents were "20,207" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L177] versus "14,161" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L179].
- Cost of expansion: depreciation and amortization was "2,674" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L291] versus "2,426" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L292].
- Gaps: planned openings, the capex budget and return on new warehouses are "not stated in the files." The release shows investment rising alongside sales but does not tie it to a stated growth plan.
Insight: Growth is concentrated in digital rather than only broad-based: digitally-enabled adjusted 52-week comps sit well above total company adjusted comps. [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L42] "20.7%" versus [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L37] "6.6%"

FUTURE DEVELOPMENTS AND STRATEGIC RECOMMENDATIONS
- Catalysts visible in the release: digital strength ("20.7%" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L42]), a larger investment base ("(6,435)" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L310]), and growing fee revenue ("5,907" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L81]). Forward guidance and the expansion pipeline are "not stated in the files."
- Watch items: the current portion of long-term debt rose to "2,248" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L227] from "75" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L228]. The Q4 tariff refund is non-recurring ("non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L44]), so it should not be extrapolated.
- Recommendation: retrieve the 10-K Items 1 and 7 before concluding on competitive advantage. They should cover member counts, renewal rates, opening plans and segment profitability, none of which can be verified from this release.
- What would change my view: my strongest conclusion is demand durability. The test is adjusted total company comparable sales in the next filing. Fiscal 2026 was "6.6%" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L37], and the fourth quarter was "6.7%" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L35]. A clear drop below that level would challenge the conclusion. It would show that headline growth of "8.4%" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L36] leaned on gasoline and currency effects rather than underlying demand.

Insight: Fourth-quarter diluted EPS of $6.75 included a one-time tariff-refund benefit that management partly reinvested in member pricing, so underlying earnings growth was somewhat lower than the headline suggests. [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L44] "This year's fourth quarter was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values."
